predecessors.name: Sasanian Empire
predecessors.text: Vistahm 'soon held sway in the entire eastern and northern quadrants of the Iranian realm', stretching from the Oxus River to Ardabil (Khosrow II and Vistahm pages)

successors.name: Sasanian Empire
successors.text: returned to Khosrow II after Vistahm's murder near Qumis and a second expedition by Smbat Bagratuni the next year

ledger.x: c. 590/1: Vistahm, Khosrow II's uncle and spahbed of the East, claims the throne and holds the north and east of Iran. Vistahm page: 'The commonly accepted dates are ca. 590-596'; the infobox gives 'King of Kings of Iran and non-Iran' 590/1-596 or 594/5-600; Howard-Johnston and Pourshariati push the outbreak to 594/5.…

c. 596: Vistahm is murdered during the battle near Qumis and the rebellion is finished. Vistahm page: he 'was murdered by Pariowk at Khosrow's urging' near Qumis (an alternative account credits his wife Gordiya); 'it required another expedition by Smbat in the next year to finally end the rebellion'. The page gives no…

wars.name: Revolt of Vistahm
wars.outcome: After several failed armies Khosrow II called on the Armenian Smbat Bagratuni, whose army engaged Vistahm near Qumis; Vistahm was murdered in the battle and Smbat's second expedition the next year ended the rebellion.

certainty.note: A rebel realm described only as 'the eastern and northern quadrants of the Iranian realm'; no frontier on either page.
